It is deeply concerning that I must repeatedly file complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to obtain remedies that are clearly required under established federal law. Additionally, the interest charge assessed on or around XX/XX/XXXX, which was posted after the account had already been misclassified or closed in error, must also be refunded in its entirety. These adjustments are necessary to restore the account to its proper standing and to ensure full compliance with applicable credit reporting and consumer protection laws. 

In its XX/XX/XXXX response to my prior CFPB complaint, Consumer Financial Protection Bureau case # XXXX, U.S. Bank stated : The error that resulted in the account being incorrectly closed occurred in XX/XX/XXXX, following a clerical error in processing a debt-management power of attorney. 


I never authorized or participated in any debt-management program. The account was closed in error without any formal written notice. For months afterward, I made regular paymentsmany above the minimum dueand my statements continued to accrue finance charges and interest even though I could no longer use the card. 

During this same period U.S. Bank repeatedly reduced my credit limit, which inflated my balance-to-limit ratio and negatively affected my credit profile. As a result, I was denied new credit by both U.S. Bank ( XX/XX/XXXX ) and XXXX XXXX Bank ( XX/XX/XXXX ). These denials cite high utilization and time since delinquency too recent, conditions created by U.S. Banks own actions. 

U.S. Bank has since restored normal reporting and applied a total of {$160.00} in credits ( {$110.00} fee waiver + {$50.00} goodwill ). While appreciated, that amount does not address the core issueinterest and finance charges that accrued during the erroneous closure period when I was prevented from using the credit line. Under the Truth in Lending Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ), the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ), and Regulation Z ( 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( e ) ), once a billing or servicing error is identified, the creditor must refund all related finance charges and fees to restore the consumer to the position they would have been in had the error not occurred.

Although my current credit reporting now appears accurate, the financial harm from U.S. Banks admitted error remains unresolved. The bank profited from interest and fees charged while I was paying responsibly but denied access to my own credit. This practice constitutes an unfair act or practice under 12 U.S.C. 5531 ( UDAAP ) because it caused substantial injury the consumer could not reasonably avoid.

As documented in attached account portal screenshot evidence, .. U.S. Bank charged monthly interest throughout the nine-month period, amounting to {$280.00}, when the account was closed to new use. These screenshots, taken directly from my online account, confirm that interest continued to accrue from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX despite the banks admitted servicing error. Under 15 U.S.C. 1666 and 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( e ), these {$280.00} in interest charges must be refunded in full. 

The banks statement that it credited late fees as a courtesy is misleading and inaccurate. Under the law, any fees or interest assessed after an account was erroneously closed or misreported must be refunded as a matter of compliance, not goodwill. Therefore, this so-called courtesy credit was not a concession, but a legal obligation, and I expect further compensation for the broader harm caused by XXXX  continued misreporting and account mishandling.

Late-Fee Refund and Remaining Restitution U.S. Bank has acknowledged its internal error and issued partial credits totaling {$160.00} ( {$110.00} in waived late fees and a {$50.00} appreciation credit ). While appreciated, these adjustments were characterized as courtesy credits rather than as required corrections under law. Under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( a ) ( 3 ) ( B ) ) and Regulation Z ( 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( e ) ( 1 ) ), when a creditor identifies a billing or servicing error, it must credit the consumers account with all finance charges, late fees, and other charges totaled above, that accrued as a result of that error. Because U.S. Bank admitted that my account was closed in error, the refunded late fees confirm the errors financial impactbut the bank remains obligated to refund all remaining interest and finance charges from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX. Treating these mandatory refunds as mere courtesy adjustments does not satisfy the corrective-action requirements of TILA/FCBA, nor does it remedy the ongoing financial harm.

Consumer complaint narrative:
CFPB, I am submitting this complaint regarding PayPal Credit, operated by Synchrony Bank, due to a continuing and deeply concerning pattern of unfair and arbitrary credit denials. Despite my ongoing and proactive efforts to build and maintain a solid financial profile, PayPal Credit has repeatedly denied my applications without providing clear reasoning, transparency, or a meaningful opportunity for reconsideration.

Over time, I have applied to PayPal Credit under circumstances where I met or exceeded typical qualifications advertised by the company. I have demonstrated steady income, consistent repayment history with other creditors, and ongoing efforts to strengthen my credit profile. Yet, PayPal Credit has never granted me a single opportunity to establish a relationship with them, even though they claim to offer credit options for a wide range of consumers, including those actively rebuilding their credit.

These repeated denials have been disheartening, discouraging, and unfair, especially given the lack of transparency about what specific criteria or factors are being used to reject my applications. The situation is not only frustratingit raises serious concerns about compliance with the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) and CFPB fair lending standards.

Concerns Regarding Fairness and Potential Discrimination In reviewing the ongoing pattern of denials, I have grown increasingly concerned that my race and other personal characteristics may have played a role in these decisions. I am aware that under federal law, creditors are prohibited from discriminating against applicants on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, marital status, or age. However, given the persistent and unexplained nature of these denialsand the fact that similarly situated consumers appear to receive approvalsI believe there may be a potential disparate impact or bias embedded in PayPal Credits credit evaluation system or internal algorithms.

If this is the case, it would represent a serious violation of federal fair lending laws, and it would warrant immediate investigation and corrective action. It is not enough for a company to issue generic denial letters that provide no substantive reasoning, while maintaining opaque internal practices that could be resulting in unintentional but unlawful discrimination.

Consumers, including myself, deserve to be treated with fairness, dignity, and equality when applying for financial products. Repeatedly being shut out without explanationespecially when ones financial profile meets general lending standardsundermines trust in both the company and the integrity of the credit system itself. Transparency and Accountability Issues Another major issue is PayPal Credits lack of transparency regarding its decision-making process. Their
adverse action notices are vague and provide no meaningful guidance for consumers seeking to improve or understand their creditworthiness. This creates a cycle where applicants are left in the dark, unable to take corrective steps or appeal a decision that feels arbitrary.

Such a lack of transparency contradicts the principles of fair lending and responsible consumer credit practices. A company that operates under a large and well-known financial brand like PayPal has an obligation to ensure its credit decision systems are transparent, equitable, and free of any discriminatory influence.

Request for CFPB Action and Investigation I am respectfully requesting that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau conduct a full investigation into PayPal Credits credit evaluation and decision-making practices. Specifically, I urge the CFPB to examine : 1. Whether PayPal Credit and Synchrony Bank are using automated systems or algorithms that produce disparate impacts on applicants of certain racial or ethnic backgrounds.

2. Whether the companys credit scoring criteria are consistent, fair, and compliant with ECOA and CFPB fair lending regulations.

3. Whether consumers are being provided with sufficient disclosure and transparency regarding the specific reasons for denial, as required under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ).

4. Whether PayPal Credits advertising and public representations about accessibility to credit align with their actual approval patterns and internal lending behavior.

If the Bureau finds evidence that these practices are discriminatory, inconsistent, or deceptive, I request that appropriate enforcement measures be taken, including but not limited to supervisory action, civil penalties, and mandatory policy reforms to ensure that all consumers are evaluated fairly.

Personal Impact These repeated denials have caused unnecessary stress and frustration. I have worked diligently to manage my finances responsibly and maintain good standing with other creditors. Being repeatedly denied by PayPal Credit, without clear explanation or an opportunity for appeal, has not only limited my financial options but has also undermined my confidence in the fairness of major financial institutions.

When a large financial entity like PayPal continues to deny credit without explanationwhile presenting itself publicly as inclusive and supportive of consumer growthit sends a message that some applicants are simply not welcome, no matter their progress or intent. That is unacceptable and inconsistent with the principles that the CFPB enforces.

Consumer complaint narrative:
CFPB, I am submitting this complaint against Klarna, the financial-technology company offering buy-now, pay-later and revolving credit products to U.S. consumers. Despite maintaining a responsible financial record and demonstrating consistent income, I have been repeatedly denied or restricted from using Klarnas credit services.

Each denial has been unexplained, vague, and unjustified, leaving me unable to understand or correct the basis for these decisions. I have made multiple attempts to engage responsibly with Klarnas platform, yet I have not been granted any opportunity to establish a credit relationship or demonstrate repayment capability.

This pattern of denial appears unfair, arbitrary, and possibly discriminatory. Klarna advertises accessibility and flexibility, but its actions have consistently excluded me without transparency or rationale.

Concerns Regarding Fair Lending and Potential Discrimination I strongly believe that my race may have influenced Klarnas credit decisions. Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) and Regulation B, creditors are prohibited from considering race, color, or national origin when making credit determinations.

Klarna relies heavily on automated decision-making algorithms that lack human oversight. These systems may be producing disparate impacts on applicants of certain racial or demographic backgrounds, resulting in systematic exclusion from credit opportunities.

It is deeply concerning that despite my stable income, responsible financial behavior, and efforts to maintain good standing with other lenders, Klarnas system continues to deny me approval without any meaningful review. This raises questions about whether Klarnas algorithms and internal models comply with fair lending principles and whether the company is exercising appropriate monitoring for algorithmic bias or disparate impact.

Consumers should not face invisible barriers simply because of automated systems that are shielded from public scrutiny.

Transparency and Accountability Issues Klarnas adverse-action notices are vague and noncompliant with the standards established under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ).

When denying an application, Klarna typically sends a short automated message such as We were unable to approve this purchase, with no details on : Which credit bureau or data source was used ; What specific factors caused the denial ; or How to dispute or verify the information.

This lack of transparency leaves consumers powerless to correct potential errors or understand the underlying decision. Such practices undermine both consumer confidence and the integrity of the broader credit system.

A fintech company operating under U.S. jurisdiction must be held to the same transparency, disclosure, and fairness standards as traditional banks. Klarnas current practices fall far short of these expectations.

Request for CFPB Investigation I am respectfully requesting that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau initiate a full and comprehensive enforcement investigation into Klarnas lending, scoring, and credit-decision practices. Specifically, I urge the Bureau to : 1. Determine whether Klarnas automated underwriting or credit-approval systems create disparate impacts based on race, national origin, or other protected classes.

2. Evaluate whether Klarnas adverse-action notices comply with FCRA requirements for specificity, accuracy, and consumer disclosure.

3. Examine Klarnas compliance with the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B, ensuring that its algorithms and data sources do not enable discrimination.

4. Assess whether Klarnas advertising representations about accessibility and inclusiveness accurately reflect its actual approval patterns.

Requested Enforcement Action Given the seriousness and persistence of these concerns, I request that the CFPB consider strong enforcement measures if violations are found. Specifically, I ask that the Bureau : 1. Impose civil penalties or sanctions against Klarna if evidence confirms discriminatory or unfair lending practices.

2. Require Klarna to undergo a comprehensive fair-lending audit conducted by independent third-party examiners.

3. Mandate corrective actions and public reporting of the companys compliance with ECOA and FCRA obligations.

4. If systemic misconduct or discrimination is verified, suspend or revoke Klarnas authority to offer consumer-credit products in the United States until full compliance and remedial action are demonstrated.

The CFPB has the responsibility to ensure that any financial entity operating within its jurisdiction treats all consumers fairly and lawfully. A company that repeatedly excludes applicants without transparency, fairness, or accountability should not be permitted to continue operating unchecked.

Personal Impact Klarnas repeated denials have caused both personal frustration and practical financial harm. I have worked hard to maintain a responsible financial record, only to face rejection by a company that claims to be inclusive. The experience has left me questioning whether I am being judged by factors unrelated to my true creditworthiness.

These arbitrary denials have limited my ability to make everyday purchases and participate fully in the modern consumer economy. It is profoundly discouraging to see a company with global resources and advanced technology treating applicants in this opaque and dismissive way.

Financial inclusion means fairness, not exclusion. No consumer should feel invisible or misjudged by algorithms that may harbor built-in bias.

b'I, XXXX XXXX XXXX, provide this sworn public statement to report a decade-long, systematic campaign of financial exploitation, identity misuse, document interception, and breach of fiduciary duty committed primarily by my brother, XXXX XXXX, that has caused catastrophic, continuing financial harm and has resulted in repeated garnishments, missing tax refunds, and the diversion of assets and benefits that were rightfully mine.

Ive spent the last decade trying to make sense of how I end up just barely financially stable with little savings only to realize I was never supposed to see the truth. What Im living through wasnt some simple mix-up or bad luck. It was orchestrated, built off access that someone I trusted  my brother  used against me.

When I was in college, juggling classes and work, I had no reason to think my accounts or documents were being touched. He always had access easy access to my personal information  my ID (temporary black and white ID found in his drawer next to my first unsigned debit card), my phone number (by extension he worked for XXXX which enabled use of my number as I saw double texts in phone bill statements), my email (relayed so even when I lost access, he may have still had access), XXXX  (logged info of passwords I couldnt remember myself I found on his laptop even after wiping memory only to come back to my account logged back on the same laptop)  and used that access in secret to monitor my every move to keep me from seeing what was being done in my name or keep access to my accounts whether it be through an OTP or temporary pin. I didnt realize how deep it went until this past summer, when I started filing CFPB complaints and demanding original records that had been withheld for years.

Thats when the pattern finally came into focus.

He kept denying he had any of our dads documents. I have the whole conversation screen recorded. He said he didnt have anything past 20 years ago. Then after I pushed him, he finally gave me the documents. The briefcase had pay stubs with retirement plan tax benefits taken out and multiple preprinted affidavit forms with blanks to fill in. These were all documents I hadnt seen before or that were only sent to me selectively.

The unclaimed benefits were in my name, but I never personally made any claim for them. He signed those papers during my first year of college. That was his first breach. I didnt get mine until a full year later, and around that same time theres a charge where I paid off all my student loans in XXXX  and another charge from a student loan service I never used. Right after that are ATM withdrawals in XXXX, Washington  somewhere I rarely went because I didnt have my license until after XXXX, and I never liked going there. The XXXX  charges stand out because there arent any other charges nearby, even though theyre ATM withdrawals, and that other large charge is also irregular.

In XXXX XXXX, an unendorsed check  my brother claimed tied to annuity lump sum from XXXX XXXX  was deposited into my XXXX  account. I had no knowledge of this. I didnt sign it, I wasnt told about it, and I didnt even know it existed. My brother led me to believe Id receive a direct deposit  never once mentioning a physical check. Later, I found out the paperwork I signed wasnt notarized, wasnt complete, and clearly wasnt structured for transparency. He had told me everything was being handled and that my portion would come through electronically. Then later was notified the CFPB and XXXX  chat simultaneously that the check was received via atm deposit, unendorsed. 


Fast-forward to when I got my hands on a XXXX  document from that same account  which clearly states it was meant to be a single cash payment. No mention of a transfer, no direct deposit. Thats when everything snapped into focus and this was a pattern. He used the banks tools and his technique with computers into order to maneuver and manipulate my account to transfer out the entirety of this lump sum in under 8 months. Then this continued with interest as I am until this day paying for it without ever being given notification as to why I am paying an invisible and seamlessly endless bill thats consistently left me financial budget until now when I have the time to look over the entirety of my finances. I started in the back of house as a prep cook then worked my way into better pay as a bartender for around 10 years.  The last thing I wanted to do when I went home and was to open my bank account and see my account inexplicably dwindle while I worked overtime. 

Now I can teach English my 300 hour tefl certificate and soon a 60 hour course on teaching business English. Before that I need to focus on the security around my life. This included. 

I started requesting records from every relevant institution  XXXX, XXXX XXXX, the IRS, and credit bureaus  and the picture only got uglier. I can now see that transactions were manipulated inside my XXXX  accounts. He was able to make things balance out visually so the theft wouldnt show up easily  deposits and withdrawals smoothed out to appear routine. Looking at those old statements now, its obvious there were split transactions, duplicate entries, and credit card transference patterns that dont reflect my actual spending or income.

The credit card under my name was found years later in his room, unsigned  and yet somehow it had been actively used. The statements dont reflect my lifestyle or my reality during that time. I was working, using my debit card, paying tuition, and living modestly  not running credit. Yet the card drained huge sums through ATM withdrawals and unauthorized spending, all while my legitimate deposits disappeared through unexplained transfers.

Then came the fallout.

Once that unendorsed check was pushed through in XXXX, I started seeing unexplained tax garnishments, offsets, and refund denials that I couldnt even contest because I had no idea what they were tied to. My first garnishment came out of nowhere. After that, it became an annual nightmare. Every year, more money was taken without explanation. Every time I tried to open a new account or rebuild, it would eventually be flagged or garnished again.

I now believe this is directly tied to the misuse of my information  and to my brothers actions with those accounts and documents. XXXX XXXX has confirmed they have no record of a payment under my fathers name or Social Security number, meaning the check he deposited was not a legitimate issue from that source. That alone shouldve stopped everything  but no one caught it.

And while all this was happening, I was out there doing everything right. I worked through college, paid off my student loans, paid down my credit cards, and even reached the best credit standing Id ever had after finally receiving my lump sum. I used it responsibly  to clear debt, stabilize, and plan for my future. But within eight months, the entire sum was gone. Between the manipulated transfers, credit card activity, and unauthorized loans, it all evaporated  leaving me with no explanation and no control.

Its hard to describe how it feels to realize the person who grew up beside you  someone you never had a serious fight with  would quietly sabotage you for years. Hes smart, tech-savvy, and knows how to manipulate systems. He has built a good life for himself and has had all the tools to do so he graduated with a XXXX XXXX degree from the XXXX XXXX XXXX and can land a solid tech job anywhere. Governmental jobs included, which may be the reason for all the resistance Im getting as Im continually led to believe this has always been my fault. He used the resources at hand and the social leverage he had over me to use and break me financially while inviting me out for an occasional expensive sushi dinner, his treat. 

Besides the betrayal, the gaslighting, the complete lack of respect or human decency, he made a lot more money than me and always had. For years, I blamed inflation and poor staff management at various jobs. Ive always worked hard at whatever I do and I usually enjoyed bartending. I had. A great paying job at one point but with my luck, a car drove through the front of the building and it closed down. A bulk of us were let go shortly after, that was XXXX XXXX in XXXX  on XXXX XXXX, Seattle. Now I can see that every mistake (except for that one, which at this point I wouldnt be surprised was something he manufactured as well) was organized deception to lead me astray in order to cover up a mess he hoped I wouldnt find. Every denial, every delay, every unexplained fee or hold  they all trace back to the same root year, XXXX. The year I had to leave college because even when I planned my budget and attended after turning XXXX, it quickly became less financially viable for me to conceive so I went back to work in Seattle. 

Ive filed reports with the CFPB, EBSA, FTC, and the FBI (though the site may have timed out since I never got a confirmation email). Ive detailed how this started, what Ive discovered, and what its cost me. Every submission, every document, every note is real  and all point to the same truth: this wasnt incompetence. It was interference.

Im no longer confused. Im angry  and Im done being quiet about it. I want accountability. I want the truth to be reflected in the record, not buried under bureaucracy or assumptions.

Because Ive done nothing wrong. Ive spent ten years paying for someone elses choices, and now that I finally understand what happened, Im not backing down until this is made right.

Put me under oath and I will answer any question truthfully and youll see that I have played no part in whats happened, I dont even really know all thats justified that continued garnishment straight from my bank account. Ill take accountability where justified but I need the same treatment for all parties involved because I did not incite the snowball effect into my own financial destruction just because I wanted to deposit a check early or make an extra $XXXX  to gain capital over my brother as result of my fathers death.

On XX/XX/year>, I was the victim of an employment-related gift card scam. I received messages from an individual impersonating my new supervisor, who instructed me to urgently purchase three {$200.00} XXXX gift cards ( totaling {$600.00} ) from XXXX XXXX in XXXX XXXX, NY. Believing this to be a legitimate work-related task, I used my Discover credit card to complete the purchase. Immediately after, I also made a {$400.00} purchase on my XXXX XXXX debit card for the same purpose. 
Shortly after making these transactions, I realized I had been deceived. The scammer had detailed personal and workplace information, leading me to believe the request was authentic. Upon realizing it was fraudulent, I took all appropriate actions : I deactivated the gift cards through XXXX before they could be used. 
I contacted XXXX XXXX, the police, and the FTC, filing formal reports. 
I submitted a fraud dispute to Discover and XXXX XXXX, providing receipts, text messages, and evidence of the scam. 
XXXX XXXX refunded my {$400.00} transaction in full, recognizing the incident as fraud. 
Discover, however, denied my {$600.00} dispute, claiming the charge was authorized since I personally made the purchasedespite my lack of intent or informed consent. 
This classification is incorrect under FTC guidelines, which explicitly recognize gift card payment scams as fraud, not consumer error. The scammer never had access to my card information, and I received no goods or services from the transaction, meaning the charge qualifies as a billing error under Regulation Z ( XXXX ). 
As a XXXX working student starting a new job, I was manipulated under false pretenses and acted immediately once the fraud became clear. I requested that Discover reopen and reinvestigate the {$600.00} dispute, issue a provisional credit, and provide a detailed written explanation of how the previous decision was reached. They rejected my dispute still under the pretenses it was authorized, although it was not as a result of fraud and deception.

Sub-issue: Problem using a debit or ATM card
Consumer complaint narrative:
My name is XXXX XXXX XXXX, and I am XXXX years old. I have been a loyal Navy Federal Credit Union member for many years. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received an official letter from Navy Federal ( Ref # XXXX ) stating that my debit card ending XXXX was suspended on XX/XX/XXXX and will remain suspended for a full year until XX/XX/XXXX because my debit-card history demonstrates a violation of the Debit Card Disclosure. ( See XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX ). 

This action has left me without electronic access to my own money and has placed me in an immediate financial crisis. 

What Happened I am an XXXXyear-old retiree living on a fixed income. My Social Security, pension, and retirement deposits are routed through my Navy Federal account. I have always been diligent and immediately reported every fraudulent transaction that appeared on my account.

Like millions of Americans, my personal information has been compromised in national data breaches that were completely beyond my control. I was the victim not the cause of those fraudulent events.

Despite my full cooperation with Navy Federals fraud department, the credit union has revoked my debit-card privileges for one year and has refused to provide any alternative means of reasonable access. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I spoke with a Navy Federal supervisor who suggested I could use a prepaid card instead. I explained that, at my age, I am not technologically savvy and do not understand app-based or reloadable systems. That solution still prevents me from safely retrieving or managing my funds and does not meet the needs of an elderly consumer. 

Because of this restriction, I must now travel to a branch in person simply to withdraw cash. The branch is not easily accessible, so I must pay for rides to and from the location. This is physically exhausting, financially burdensome, and unsafe. Carrying cash home each time exposes me to serious risk of theft or loss. 

It will take at least two pay cycles to transfer my pension and retirement deposits to a different institution. Until then, I am effectively locked out of my income, unable to pay bills or purchase necessities safely. 

Violations and Regulatory Concerns 1. Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA, 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq. ) Navy Federals own Debit Card Disclosure ( 6 Liability for Failure to Complete Electronic Fund Transfers ) promises to complete authorized transfers correctly By disabling my card for a year, Navy Federal has denied me the ability to perform lawful electronic fund transfers, violating the EFTAs guarantee of consumer access to electronic payments.

2. Unfair and Abusive Practice ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 ; CFPB UDAAP Standards ) A blanket one-year debit-card suspension for a verified fraud victim causes substantial, unavoidable harm and serves no legitimate purpose. It is an unfair and abusive act, especially when applied to an XXXX consumer who acted responsibly and cooperated fully. 

XXXX. Breach of Good Faith and Fair Dealing ( 11 Ownership and Cancellation ) While Navy Federal reserves the right to revoke cards at any time, that discretion must still be exercised in good faith. Enforcing a year-long ban without review or accommodation is arbitrary, punitive, and contrary to the implied covenant of fair dealing. 

XXXX. Age-Based Disparate Impact ( Equal Credit Opportunity Act, 15 U.S.C. 1691 ) Younger members who experience fraud are routinely reissued cards after verification. Denying an XXXX senior a replacement constitutes age-based disparate treatment, intentional or not. 

XXXX. Elder Financial Exploitation and Accessibility ( CFPB Bulletin 2016-07 ) Federal guidance directs financial institutions to protect not endanger older adults. Forcing me to handle cash and rely on unfamiliar technology increases my exposure to theft, fraud, and hardship, directly contradicting CFPB elder-protection policy. 

Why Immediate Action Is Required I can not survive for two months without safe, convenient access to my income. I depend on my debit card to purchase groceries, medication, and essential items.

Navy Federals actions are unreasonable, harmful, and discriminatory. Leaving an elderly woman without a debit card for a year is indefensible and places me at serious financial and personal risk.

Requested Relief I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau require Navy Federal Credit Union to : Immediately reinstate my debit-card access or issue a new monitored, low-limit, or chip-protected card within 10 business days.

Provide a written explanation detailing the justification and policy authority for a one-year suspension.

Offer reasonable senior accommodations that do not depend on prepaid or app-based tools.

Reimburse documented transportation or service costs incurred while accessing funds during this restriction.

Conduct a policy review ensuring Navy Federals fraud-prevention measures comply with EFTA and do not unfairly impact elderly or vulnerable members.

In conclusion, This matter is urgent. Navy Federal has knowingly placed an XXXX consumer in financial jeopardy by denying access to her own funds for a year, despite clear evidence that she was the victim of data breaches and not the cause of fraud. 

I ask the CFPB to intervene immediately, enforce compliance with federal consumer-protection laws, and compel Navy Federal Credit Union to restore my debit-card access without delay. 

Thank you for your prompt attention and protection of senior consumers like me.

Each time Im told the dispute was filed too late and can not be reopened. Capital One has not provided a clear written explanation of its findings or confirmed that my evidence was ever reviewed. 

Under Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.13 ( b ) ( 1 ), the 60-day period for reporting a billing error begins after the first periodic statement on which the error appeared is transmitted to the consumer. The CFPBs Official Interpretation clarifies that this deadline applies only once a consumer could reasonably identify an error from the information provided. Because the service failure was not apparent until months after billing, the alleged error was not discoverable within 60 days. 

Furthermore, Regulation Z 1026.13 ( f ) requires a reasonable investigation and a fair opportunity for the consumer to present information. Reliance on a single unconfirmed email that went to spam does not constitute reasonable notice. 

I am requesting that Capital One be directed to reopen or reinvestigate the dispute, review the documentation I have supplied, and issue a written explanation of findings in compliance with Regulation Z and the Fair Credit Billing Act.

Overview of the Issue This is a new and expanded complaint concerning Synchrony XXXX deceptive and misleading administration of a 0 % APR for 24 months personal loan, which I obtained in XX/XX/XXXX, and the banks subsequent failure to address my core concerns in CFPB case # XXXX. 

The original complaint explained that Synchronys minimum payment display, online interface, and verbal customer support guidance misled me into believing that I was paying my promotional loan correctly and on pace to satisfy the full payoff conditions within the XXXX period. Despite paying faithfully every month, Synchrony ultimately imposed retroactive interest on the entire {$25000.00} loan, nearly doubling my balance and erasing two years of payments. 

Synchronys previous CFPB response completely ignored the substantive issues raised. It cited fine-print contract language instead of addressing the deceptive structure and administration of its payment system. I am refiling to request that the CFPB conduct a formal reinvestigation and systemic review of Synchronys deferred-interest loan practices. 

Detailed Chronology of Events 1. Loan Origination XX/XX/XXXX In XX/XX/XXXX, I opened a personal loan with Synchrony XXXX for {$25000.00}. The loan was heavily advertised and represented as a 0 % APR for 24 months promotional offer. I accepted this offer with the clear understanding that if I made my monthly payments as directed, I would pay off the balance without incurring interest. 

When setting up the loan by phone with a Synchrony representative in XX/XX/XXXX, I specifically asked about the payment requirements and was advised that the monthly minimum payment displayed on the account portal would keep me compliant with the promotional terms. There was no mention or warning that the minimum payment would be insufficient to retire the loan by the end of the XXXX period. 

2. Payment History XXXX to XXXX Throughout the entire promotional period, I made consistent monthly payments of approximately {$630.00}, following Synchronys own online prompts and billing statements which clearly labeled this as the Minimum Payment Due. 
Each month, I logged into my Synchrony account and paid the exact minimum amount displayed. 

At no point during these two years did Synchrony issue any communication, warning, or disclosure suggesting that I was not on pace to satisfy the full balance within the 0 % promotional period. 

In late XXXX, I proactively called Synchrony customer service again to confirm that I was paying correctly. The representative verified that my account was in good standing, my payments were appropriate, and I was on track. 

This communication reinforced my good-faith belief that I was fulfilling all promotional requirements. 

3. Expiration of the Promotional Period Late XXXX At the end of the XXXX term, I was shocked to discover that, despite my consistent XXXX XXXX monthly payments, I still owed approximately {$10000.00} in remaining principal. Immediately thereafter, Synchrony applied two years of retroactive interest on the entire {$25000.00} principal, resulting in a balance that now exceeds {$23000.00}. 

This outcome effectively erased all progress made over two years of diligent payments. It transformed what had been marketed as an interest-free offer into a debt trap with retroactive interest that would not have accrued had Synchrony clearly disclosed the real payment requirements or honored its representatives verbal guidance. 

Synchronys Inadequate Response to CFPB Case # XXXX In response to my original CFPB complaint, Synchrony provided a generic and dismissive reply. The bank simply restated contract language that interest would apply if the balance was not paid in full by the end of the promotional period. 

This response is wholly non-responsive to the substance of my complaint. Synchrony failed to address any of the following key points : The Misleading Minimum Payment Feature Synchronys payment interface and billing statements explicitly present a Minimum Payment Due amount. The logical interpretation of that termparticularly for a 0 % promotional offeris that paying the minimum keeps the loan in good standing under the promotional terms. By ignoring all of these issues, Synchronys response violates the spirit of CFPB Complaint Process XXXX, requiring that regulated institutions respond substantively and in good faith. 

Legal and Regulatory Framework This case raises issues under multiple federal consumer protection laws and regulations : 1. Truth in Lending Act ( TILA, 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ) TILA mandates that all terms of a credit arrangement be clearly and conspicuously disclosed. Synchronys use of a minimum payment that could never satisfy the promotional payoff requirement, without explicit disclosure to that effect, violates this requirement.

2. Regulation Z ( 12 CFR 1026 ) Regulation Z requires that any promotional or deferred-interest offer must clearly describe : The conditions required to retain the promotional rate ; The consequences of failing to meet those conditions ; and Any minimum payment structure that might cause loss of the promotion.

Synchronys interface, billing statements, and representative guidance did not provide this information clearly, conspicuously, or consistently. 

3. Dodd-Frank Act 1031 UDAAP Provisions The Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) provisions prohibit lenders from engaging in conduct that misleads or is likely to mislead consumers. A reasonable consumer, seeing minimum payment due and receiving verbal assurance of compliance, would assume they were satisfying the requirements of a 0 % APR offer. Synchronys structure is therefore deceptive and unfair under federal law. 

4. State UDAP Laws ( e.g., [ Your State ] Consumer Protection Act ) Most states, including [ Your State ], have similar prohibitions against deceptive trade practices. Synchronys actionsespecially the misrepresentation of a promotional offer through its interface and verbal guidancelikely violate state consumer-protection statutes as well.

Why Synchronys Practice Is Systemically Harmful I am not the only consumer affected by this design. Public CFPB complaint records, consumer-advocacy websites, and financial forums contain dozens of similar complaints describing identical experiences : Borrowers take out a Synchrony 0 % loan or credit promotion. 

They pay the displayed minimum payment faithfully. 

At the end of the promotional period, they are informed that the balance was not fully paid and that deferred interest has now been applied retroactively. 

This pattern strongly suggests a systemic, profit-driven model based on deferred interest accrual. The payment interface and customer communications are structured to maximize the likelihood that consumers will inadvertently trigger the retroactive interest clause, allowing Synchrony to collect thousands of dollars in back-interest after two years of interest-free marketing claims. 

Such practices undermine the intent of consumer credit transparency laws and exploit ordinary consumers good-faith reliance on lender representations.

Broader Public Interest Synchrony Bank is one of the largest private-label and promotional credit providers in the U.S., servicing millions of consumers. If the CFPB permits Synchrony to continue structuring its 0 % APR and deferred-interest programs in this way, the harm will extend far beyond this single case. 

The pattern described here represents a structural deception built into Synchronys product designa deliberate reliance on misleading payment structures that virtually guarantee consumer default on promotional conditions. 

By investigating and addressing this practice, the CFPB has an opportunity to protect a significant portion of American borrowers who are similarly being misled. 

Conclusion Synchrony Banks conduct in this matter was deceptive, unfair, and harmful. Its failure to meaningfully respond to CFPB complaint # XXXX underscores its unwillingness to engage in good-faith dispute resolution.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint against Wells Fargo Bank , N.A . for unfair, arbitrary, and repeated denials of my credit card applications and for the companys continued failure to demonstrate transparency, fairness, or accountability in its credit decision-making processes. 

Despite my continued efforts to build and maintain responsible credit, Wells Fargo has repeatedly issued rejections that are unsupported by evidence and unexplained in substance. This pattern of behavior has crossed the line from poor customer service to a potential regulatory violation, and it demonstrates that this banks internal credit and compliance systems are either deeply flawed or willfully discriminatory. 



Background and Pattern of Conduct After submitting my most recent credit card application, Wells Fargo sent me yet another generic denial letter claiming I did not meet the companys credit criteria. The letter provided no detailed reasoning, offered no transparency, and failed to identify which specific factors were responsible for the decision. 

This lack of explanation is not consistent with the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) or Regulation B, both of which require lenders to give consumers specific reasons for adverse credit actions. Simply stating credit criteria not met or credit score too low without identifying factual context is not an acceptable or compliant disclosure.

I have reason to believe that Wells Fargos internal approval models and manual review practices may be discriminatory, arbitrary, or selectively designed to reject certain consumer segments without valid cause. Such practices undermine public confidence in the b
anking system and violate the principles of transparency that the CFPB was established to enforce.

Consumer Harm This repeated and baseless denial has caused both financial and emotional harm. I have taken deliberate, consistent steps to maintain strong credit hygiene paying accounts on time, maintaining low utilization, and avoiding negative marks. Yet, despite these efforts, Wells Fargo continues to deny my applications while offering no opportunity for remediation or explanation.

This has tangible consequences : 1. Financial setback : Each denial negatively impacts my ability to diversify my credit portfolio and advance toward financial goals. It directly affects my access to fair credit opportunities available to others with similar or even weaker profiles.

2. Emotional distress and frustration : Being continually rejected without cause fosters a sense of helplessness and discouragement. It creates the impression that Wells Fargos decisions are predetermined and unchallengeable, regardless of m
erit.

3. Market distortion : When a large national bank unfairly restricts access to credit, it effectively suppresses consumer mobility and limits the competitive fairness that the CFPB seeks to promote.

Lack of Transparency and Regulatory Accountability Wells Fargos behavior is not new. This institution has a long, public record of regulatory infractions including consent orders, fines, and enforcement actions that point to chronic governance failures. Despite repeated regulatory scrutiny, the company has not reformed its internal decision-making culture. 

The CFPBs statutory mandate under 12 U.S.C. 55315536 grants authority to act against unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ). Wells Fargos repeated pattern of opaque credit denials and refusal to disclose factual reasoning constitutes an unfair and deceptive practice, especially when consumers are systematically denied access to credit without explanation.

Transparency and accountability are not optional features they are legal obligations under federal law. Wells Fargos consistent failure to comply with these obligations warrants immediate intervention.

The Citi Rep questioned me for several minutes, sent several codes to my phone and asked the challenge questions for which I provided the correct responses. Afterwards, she informed me that I should have online access through the Citibank Mobile App in a few minutes. 

After 20 minutes, I attempted online access. I received another Citibank text that, in order to gain access, I could anticipate a code which I would be required to enter on the app. When I received the text, I quickly noticed that the phone number attached to it had been changed and did not belong to me. I panicked! I called Citibank and remained on the phone line with the Citi Rep for the next hour. The Citi Rep explained that he could not help me due to the mismatched information and directed me to visit a Citibank branch in person. 

That afternoon on XX/XX/XXXX, I drove to the XXXX Citibank Branch to report the lost wallet and the suspected fraud. The XXXX Citibank Branch Manager, XXXX XXXX XXXX, replied that she could not help me due to the fact that I had no official identification, and directed me to speak with the Fraud Dept. I attempted to present my replacement Drivers License, XXXX Police Report and employee ID to establish my identity. XXXX dismissed these items, and quickly and abruptly insisted that I speak with the Fraud dept. She escorted me to a conference where she phoned the Fraud dept and handed the phone receiver to me.

After listening to the circumstances about the lost wallet and suspected fraud, the Fraud Dept Citi Rep. reviewed my account and asked if I recognized several transactions, which I did not. She stated that my account was compromised and that a new Citi bankcard would be delivered through the XXXX overnight services. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I did not report to work and waited for the Citi bankcard to arrive. It was important to me to immediately reactivate my Citibank card in order to pay bills and to purchase groceries. To my dismay, the Citibank card was not delivered within the 24 hours that was promised by the Fraud Dept Rep. Instead, it arrived during the following afternoon on Saturday, XX/XX/XXXX. Upon receipt, I immediately attempted to activate it, but it did not work. I was unable to visit the XXXX XXXX for assistance as the banking hours had already ended. Therefore, I was placed in the position of borrowing cash over the weekend to pay bills and to buy groceries.

The Personal Banker, XXXX XXXX, asked me to insert the card into the card reader, but it did not activate. XXXX reviewed my account and provided 4 digits which she indicated were attached to my new checking account. I was confused? I was unaware of a new checking account. XXXX explained that the Fraud or Customer Dept had created the checking account over the weekend. I asked XXXX details about the fraudulent transactions, but she indicated that she could not discuss the specifics due to the restrictions on the account. Her response intrigued me on the basis that she had already provided the last 4 digits of this mysterious newly created checking account. 

I was escorted to a conference room. XXXX phoned the Fraud dept and explained to me that the Fraud Depts role is to review unauthorized transactions. The Fraud Citibank Representative was very difficult to understand due to the background chatter and the individuals accent. I discontinued the conversation and phoned back in the hopes of speaking with a Citibank Rep that I could better understand. During this conversation, I could understand a little better, but not much. The CitibankFraud Rep confirmed that the account had been compromised and had been closed to prevent further fraud. I was completely devastated to hear this news! As I reflected, I reviewed all the steps I had taken to avoid the fraud from occurring with my checking account. 1 ) I phoned Citibank immediately and notified the Citi Rep of possible fraud when I realized I lost my wallet. 2 ) I took the day off from work and waited all day for the Citi bankcard 3 ) I presented my replacement Drivers License as evidence of my identity. How could this have happened? I informed XXXX that XXXX practices were not supportive of me and contributed to the scammers successful access into my checking account, resulting in the fraudulent transactions and my inability to handle my financial responsibilities. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I visited the Citibank XXXX XXXX to follow up with the Manager, XXXX XXXX , in the hopes of an exception to the policy and the acceptance of my replacement Drivers License. She was adamant that there was nothing she could do. I reiterated that I had taken all the necessary steps to prevent the unauthorized access of my checking account. XXXX response was that it is the Fraud Depts responsibility to place the restriction and that there must have been some miscommunication. I let XXXX know that I have been with Citibank for 37 years and that I should qualify for an exception to the requirement to present the official Drivers License, and therefore, to allow the replacement. There was no empathy or support. I left, but I was determined to get clear answers on why this problem occurred. 

In the meantime, I received a Citi mobile app notification that the 2nd Citibank card was scheduled to be delivered. Soon after the Fraud Dept notification, I was informed by XXXX from the XXXX Branch that the 2nd Citibank card would not be valid due to its attachment to the compromised checking account. Because the scammer continued to have access to my Citi mobile account, he/she received Citi app updates and was aware of the delivery. The scammer staked out in front of my address and intercepted the 2nd Citi bankcard. It became clear to me that the Fraud Dept had not blocked the scammer from receiving mobile updates.

229.13 ( g ) ( 2 ) When the reason for delay changes, the bank must provide a new written notice. None was given when the hold became a suspense transfer.

In USAAs prior response, the bank stated that the disputed transactions from XXXX XXXX XXXX were authorized because the chip was read and because I had the card in my possession. These statements are not a regulatory basis for assigning cardholder liability. Regulation Z does not permit denial of a billing-error claim solely on the basis of physical card possession or chip usage.

Additionally, on XX/XX/year>, USAA issued a {$320.00} internal remediation payment tied to prior dispute handling. This action contradicts its claim that all procedures were followed correctly and indicates that an internal control issue or error existed. 
Finally, my attempt to obtain written communication from the executive-office email address provided was unsuccessful, and the email bounced. This prevented me from receiving timely written acknowledgment as contemplated under 1026.13 ( d ) ( 1 ).

Requested Regulatory Action I respectfully request that the CFPB : Determine whether USAA met its obligations under 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( f ) to conduct a reasonable investigation, including review of time, location, and merchant-sequencing evidence.

Determine whether denial based on chip read and post-event card possession constitutes a compliant liability assignment.

Require USAA to produce : Merchant timestamps Merchant location data Internal investigation notes Any communications with merchants or processors Require full remediation of the remaining disputed amount ( {$440.00} ), including any related interest and fees.

Review whether USAAs internal remediation event suggests systemic dispute-handling deficiencies.

USAA : Did not provide timestamp/location evidence, Relied on non-regulatory rationales, Did not produce requested investigation documentation, Issued partial remediation inconsistent with its denial, Failed to acknowledge physical impossibility, And relied solely on internal policy/verbal assertions.

Citibank staff refused to provide information on why this information was required, why they were contacting our organization and simply demanded I appear at a branch to resolve this or they would deny access to our funds. I am continuing to attempt to resolve this, but am uncomfortable with demands for personal information without justification. 

In XX/XX/year>, our organization attempted in good faith to comply with Citibanks Know Your Customer ( KYC ) requirements, yet the process was marked by repeated missteps, conflicting guidance, and unnecessary burdens on our staff. Without prior notice, our accounts were blocked, leaving us unable to conduct normal business transactions and requiring more than 20 hours of senior staff time on calls with Citibank representatives. We have experienced redundant requests for information already on file, contradictory directions from staff that forced repeated resubmissions, and quality review demands that changed without explanation. We were directed to provide information that was either inaccurate or irrelevant, and at one point our Chief Financial Officer was forced to spend six hours at a branch correcting errors caused by Citibanks own processes. Compounding these issues, communication has been slow or nonexistent, escalation paths limited, and technology systems within Citibank appear unable to share basic customer information. The cumulative effect has been an undue hardship on our team and a serious disruption to our banking operations, for which we expect both immediate resolution and assurance that these failures will not recur. 
________________________________________ Examples of Issues Encountered Redundant Information Requests : Citibank staff repeatedly requested information already on file, including lists of authorized signers and personal identification. These details were required verbally at the start of each call, yet still had to be resubmitted via forms from scratch. 
Contradictory Staff Guidance : Forms completed per Citibank staff instructions were later rejected by analysts as incorrect, forcing resubmission of all documentation. Each cycle required re-entering the same data from the beginning. 
Inconsistent Quality Review : Forms deemed sufficient by call representatives were subsequently rejected by Quality Assurance, which demanded new information or revisions without consistent rationale.

Incorrect Legal References : Citibank Staff cited non-existent rules or laws as the basis for certain requests, only to later concede the information was unnecessary. 
Delayed and Inadequate Notification : Accounts were blocked by analysts without prior warning. Outbound Citibank stafftasked with notifying customersoperated with little urgency, often delaying outreach by up to five days. In some cases, no notification to our organization occurred at all. 
Lack of Escalation Options : Customers can not escalate issues to the analysts who enact account blocks. The only escalation channel leads to Outbound staff with no authority to resolve core problems.

Unreasonable Demands on Staff Availability : On one occasion, we were informed on a Friday at noon that accounts would be re-blocked unless information was submitted immediately. With signers unavailable, the only option presented was for a senior official to drive to a branch and hand-complete forms already submitted electronically. This six-hour ordeal consumed significant executive time unnecessarily. 
Requests for False or Irrelevant Information : Staff at times directed us to enter information we knew to be false, which we refused. Other requests included providing irrelevant details, such as the address of the U.S. Department of State.

Disjointed Systems : Branch systems are not integrated with KYC systems. For example, all signers completed account setup in person at a branch without the branch manager being aware that the account was already blocked.

Technology Failures : The Docusign process failed to accommodate required actions, leading to document rejections even when we followed system rules. This forced yet another complete restart of forms. 

Please note that we are a 40 year customer of Citibank and funded by Congressional Action.

Consumer complaint narrative:
CFPB, Summary of Complaint I am filing this complaint to report Affirm, Inc. for repeated and unjustified credit denials, deceptive and misleading marketing, and a complete lack of transparency in their decision-making process. Affirm presents itself to consumers as a simple, fair, and accessible financing platform allowing individuals to shop now and pay later. However, my repeated experience with this company demonstrates a pattern of conduct that appears deceptive, arbitrary, and harmful to consumers. 

Despite being an existing and verified customer, Affirm continues to deny me credit, often instantly and without explanation. Each time I attempt to make a purchase through Affirms app or a partner merchant, my request is declined with a vague message such as You do not qualify at this time. No valid reasoning is provided, no adverse action notice is sent, and no opportunity for clarification or correction is offered. 

This process is deeply frustrating and unfair. It misleads consumers into believing that approval for Affirms service means ongoing access to credit, when in practice, Affirms algorithmic systems repeatedly and arbitrarily deny legitimate consumers with no transparency. 



Detailed Narrative I originally joined Affirm because of its reputation for being a straightforward and transparent company offering accessible installment loans. Affirms marketing, app design, and messaging create the impression that once approved, a consumer can continue to use the service responsibly as long as payments are made on time and the account remains in good standing. 

However, that is not the reality. Over multiple attempts, Affirm has repeatedly refused to extend financing for even small purchases, despite the fact that I have maintained my account properly. Each denial occurs automatically, with a generic message and no human review or explanation. 

These denials have occurred across multiple partner stores, with no indication that anything is wrong with my account or financial standing. Affirm does not send any formal communication explaining why I was denied, nor do they provide the required adverse action notice under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) and Regulation B. 

This omission is significant because such notices are legally required when a creditor denies a consumer application for credit. Affirms refusal to provide these notices leaves consumers in the dark about whether inaccurate data, algorithmic bias, or discriminatory practices are influencing their decisions. 

Affirms refusal to offer transparency deprives consumers of the opportunity to understand or contest unfair credit decisions, which directly violates the principles of fair lending and responsible credit reporting that federal law protects. 



Deceptive and Misleading Practices Affirms promotional statements suggest that once a user has been approved and demonstrates good repayment behavior, they will be eligible for future financing. Yet in practice, even responsible users are frequently and arbitrarily denied. 

This inconsistency between Affirms public representations and its actual credit practices is deceptive and misleading. The companys marketing gives consumers a false impression of control and stability over their access to credit. 

Moreover, the denials occur through opaque, automated systems that provide no meaningful recourse. There is no way to appeal a denial, contact a decision-maker, or understand the factors influencing the rejection. This lack of transparency and accountability is inconsistent with federal consumer protection laws. 



Potential Legal and Regulatory Concerns 1. Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) Affirm appears to be failing to provide proper adverse action notices required when denying credit. Consumers have a right to know the reasons for credit denials to correct errors or address any discriminatory outcomes.

2. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) If Affirms denials are based on information from consumer reports or alternative data sources, they are required to disclose this to consumers, which they fail to do.

3. UDAAP Violations ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 5536 ) Affirms conduct may constitute unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices. Misrepresenting continued credit availability, failing to explain denials, and concealing algorithmic decision-making all qualify as potential UDAAP violations.

These practices, taken together, point toward systemic misconduct rather than isolated error. Affirms algorithmic credit model lacks human oversight and fails to meet the transparency standards expected of regulated financial entities operating under federal law. 



Emotional and Financial Impact These repeated denials have caused considerable stress and frustration. Affirms system leaves consumers feeling powerless, confused, and misled. It undermines trust in digital lending platforms and causes unnecessary embarrassment and disruption when attempting legitimate purchases. 

The experience also creates financial uncertainty consumers can not plan purchases or manage budgets if approvals are arbitrary and unexplained. Affirms refusal to communicate reasoning or offer corrective options leaves users feeling deceived and discriminated against. 

I have lost trust in Affirm and feel that its continued operation, under its current opaque credit system, poses a risk to consumers who rely on fair access to financing.

Dear CFPB Representative, I am submitting a formal complaint regarding the restriction placed on my Bank of America credit card accounts ending in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Approximately two years ago, these accounts were restricted after I submitted a payment using a negotiable instrument recognized under the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) as a lawful form of payment.

Colorado consumer protection statutes also reinforce these rights. Regulation Z ( 12 CFR 1026.2 ( a ) ( 12 ) ) clearly defines consumer credit as being extended for personal, family, or household purposes. The restriction on my account, however, occurred without prior notice or clear justification, despite my attempt to perform lawfully under the terms of the agreement. The timing and rationale of the notice I did receive did not provide any meaningful explanation as to why a good faith attempt to satisfy the obligation would result in closure or restriction. 

Additionally, it is my understanding, both under UCC guidelines and the terms and conditions of my agreement, that if a negotiable instrument is not accepted, it must be returned to the sender ( which it was not ). Nowhere in the agreement did it state that attempting to perform on a contractual obligation using a lawful instrument would result in closure or restriction of the account. I acted in good faith to honor the agreement and was not informed that such performance could result in punitive action. 

Furthermore, according to Bank of Americas own SEC filings, I am aware that my account obligation is being bought, sold, and securitized on the secondary market, which contributes to the institutions revenue. To deny me access to the credit line extended through my original application while still profiting through securitization and continuing to receive Federal Reserve Note payments from me constitutes unjust enrichment. I am simply seeking equitable treatment and access to the account Ive maintained in good faith, or in the alternative, a full accounting and remedy. 

Despite the account restrictions, I have continued making payments in good faith and have maintained a positive payment history. I am not attempting to evade responsibility, I am asserting my right to lawful performance and fair treatment. I am fully prepared to provide documentation upon request.

Dear XXXX XXXX and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Thank you for your XX/XX/year> letter regarding my complaint. While I appreciate the summary provided, I must formally dispute the findings and request that this case be reopened for full review. 

1. I Unenrolled from Overdraft in XX/XX/year> Yet Fees Continue According to Wells Fargos own records, a courtesy refund was issued on XX/XX/year>. Immediately thereafter, I unenrolled from Standard Overdraft Protection via online banking to prevent further overdrafts. Despite that explicit opt-out, Wells Fargo has continued to process transactions that overdraw my account, resulting in repeated overdraft fees. 

Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.17 ( Regulation E ), a financial institution may not assess overdraft fees on ATM or debit-card transactions without the consumers affirmative opt-in. By continuing to honor transactions and charge fees after my documented unenrollment, Wells Fargo appears to have violated federal consumer-protection law and its own public disclosures. 

2. Declined Transactions Later Approved Without Consent I have verified that certain merchants most notably XXXX repeatedly submit the same payment authorization request after initial declines. For example, when a transaction is declined two times, XXXX will automatically resubmit the same charge across all cards on file until it finds an approval. 

Wells Fargos systems have, on multiple occasions, approved these third-attempt submissions after issuing initial decline responses. This results in unauthorized posting of a previously declined charge and subsequent overdraft fees. 

Once a transaction has been declined, it should not be processed again without explicit consumer re-authorization. Allowing resubmission and approval after a decline particularly for customers unenrolled from overdraft services undermines Regulation E protections and constitutes a failure of the banks authorization controls. 

3. Posting Order and Transparency Issues Wells Fargos own letter acknowledges that deposits and debits may post in unpredictable order depending on merchant submission. When combined with continued overdraft coverage after unenrollment, this creates systemic unpredictability that exposes consumers to fees they could not reasonably avoid. 

The fact that these issues persist after my opt-out demonstrates that the banks systems are either not honoring customer selections or not properly synchronizing authorization and posting logic. 

4. Requested Actions I respectfully request that Wells Fargo and the CFPB : Reopen this case and investigate why overdraft fees continued after unenrollment. 

Provide a complete transaction audit ( including timestamps of authorization and settlement ) for all overdraft events from XX/XX/year> to XX/XX/year>, with the exception of the {$100.00} that Wells Fargo refunded in XXXX. Refund {$2000.00} in fees resulting from these improper overdraft events. 

Confirm in writing that my account is now fully excluded from all overdraft services and that no negative marks will be reported during the investigation. 

5. Regulatory and Compliance Concerns Given Wells Fargos history of enforcement actions related to overdraft practices, this matter raises broader questions about ongoing compliance with CFPB and OCC orders. I respectfully request that the CFPB review this case for potential systemic issues affecting other consumers who have opted out yet continue to experience similar overdraft activity. 

Conclusion I appreciate your attention to this matter and request a written response confirming receipt and reopening of the case. I will provide additional transaction details or screenshots upon request. 

Thank you for your commitment to transparency and consumer fairness. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative:
CFPB Complaint : Huntington Bank Improper Stop Payment and Reversal of Cleared Check Summary : Huntington Bank improperly reversed a deposited check after it had fully cleared, citing a stop payment that was allegedly placed after final payment had already occurred. This action violates the final payment provisions of the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC 4-215 ( a ) ) and caused direct financial harm. 

Details : On XX/XX/year>, I deposited a check for {$1800.00} into my Huntington Bank account. The check was accepted, processed, and credited to my account balanceindicating that the payor bank had honored the item and that final payment had occurred under UCC 4-215 ( a ). 

On XX/XX/year>, XXXX posted a debit to my account labeled Returned Deposit Item {$1800.00}. When I contacted customer service, a supervisor named XXXX stated that the reversal was due to a stop payment on the check itself. This explanation is legally inaccurate : a stop-payment order can only be placed before an item clears ; once settlement occurs through the Federal Reserve clearing system, the transaction is final and can not be revoked by the payor bank.

I specifically requested documentation showing ( 1 ) when the stop-payment order was entered and ( 2 ) whether the item had already cleared through the clearinghouse at that time. Huntington refused to provide this information. The representative also refused to give her full name or employee identification number, preventing proper documentation of the call.

Why this is a problem : If Huntington allowed a payor bank to reverse funds after final payment, it violated the UCCs finality rule and deprived me of funds that had already been legally settled. The banks explanation ( stop payment on the check itself ) was both incorrect and misleading. Huntingtons refusal to investigate or provide documentation further raises concerns about compliance with banking transparency and consumer-protection standards.
