[What happened]
On December 19, 2024 Comenity Capital Bank sent an adverseaction letter denying my XXXX  Visa Signature application. The letter stated only: Inability to verify your previous credit experience. It also included a purported credit score disclosure that said the score was not able to be calculated and listed a score range of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXhile simultaneously stating the decision was based on information in my consumer report.

Why this is a problem

Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B a creditor must provide a written adverseaction notice that either (a) states the specific principal reason(s) for denial or (b) informs the applicant of the right to request those reasons; the notice must identify principal creditworthiness factors, not vague internal process failures. Comenitys single phrase is vague, nonspecific, and appears to describe an internal verification failure rather than a consumer creditworthiness factor.

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and Regulation V, when an adverse action is based in whole or in part on a consumer report the creditor must disclose the numerical credit score used (if any), the score range, the date of the score, the key factors affecting the score, the CRA name and contact information, and notice of the right to obtain a free report within 60 days. Comenitys XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  and was not able to be calculated statement are nonsensical and inconsistent with its statement that the decision was based on a consumer report. The listed most significant factors repeat the same vague phrase and do not identify score factors.

I provided written authorization, made myself available for account-holder authentication, and requested written transaction confirmation from XXXX XXXX XXXX Chase has refused to accept reasonable alternative verification methods while continuing to hold my funds.

Importantly, Chases initiation of account closure, its representation that a cashiers check had been issued, its subsequent reversal of that position, and its continued withholding of funds all occurred after I engaged in protected consumer activity by filing a CFPB complaint. The timing and nature of these actions raise serious concerns regarding retaliatory or unfair conduct following that complaint. 

Chases conduct reflects a pattern of moving requirements after account closure, misrepresentation regarding the status of funds, lack of custodial transparency, and unreasonable detention of customer money without explanation.

Re : Complaint Against JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . 
Product : Checking Account / Debit Card Issue : Fraud / Unauthorized Transactions Reference Number : XXXX Dear Sir or Madam : I submit this complaint to request review and intervention regarding JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.s denial of four unauthorized ATM withdrawals totaling {$1600.00} from my checking account. Chase denied these claims solely because a correct PIN was used, despite extensive evidence of criminal activity, incapacitation, lack of authorization, and my timely reporting. 

I. Background On XX/XX/year>, while traveling in XXXX, XXXX, I was drugged and robbed. My debit card, mobile phones, credit cards, and identification were stolen. I regained consciousness the following morning and did not have possession of my debit card or phone when the disputed ATM withdrawals occurred. 

XXXX. Reporting and Investigation Despite delays caused by the theft of my phones and compromise of my email account, I notified JPMorgan Chase Bank of the fraudulent activity by XX/XX/year>. I filed a criminal report by XX/XX/year>. Chase initially issued provisional credit. 
On or around XX/XX/year>, Chase reversed four ATM withdrawals while ruling other disputed transactions from the same incident in my favor. 

XXXX. Chases Denial Rationale On XX/XX/year>, I spoke with a Claims agent named XXXX and escalated to a Floor Supervisor named XXXX. XXXX XXXX stated that Chase policy treats correct PIN usage as dispositive and does not consider such transactions unauthorized. 
This rationale fails to account for coercion, incapacitation, or criminal extraction of PIN information, all of which negate actual authorization. 

IV. Transactions at Issue XX/XX/year> {$530.00} XX/XX/year> {$180.00} XX/XX/year> {$470.00} XX/XX/year> {$470.00} Total : {$1600.00} V. Regulation XXXX Concerns Under Regulation E, 12 C.F.R. 1005.2 ( m ), unauthorized electronic fund transfers are those made without actual authority. Regulation E does not equate correct PIN usage with authorization, particularly where the PIN is obtained through criminal means.

12 C.F.R. 1005.6 and 1005.11 require timely notice protections and a reasonable investigation. Chase relied on automated decisioning and a categorical PIN-based policy, rather than a good-faith investigation of the facts.

VI. Requested Resolution I request that the CFPB require JPMorgan Chase Bank to reverse its denial, reimburse {$1600.00}, and review its internal policies for compliance with Regulation E.

Consumer complaint narrative:
This issue is not isolated. I have experienced similar card authorization failures with Avant in the past, in which my account displayed available credit yet repeatedly declined at point-of-sale terminals, followed by customer support assurances that the card would function normally without disclosure of the actual cause. The recurrence of this conduct suggests a pattern rather than a one-time error. 

Despite my repeated requests for clarification and escalation, Avant representatives consistently provided scripted recitations of declined transactions already known to me, rather than substantive information regarding the cause of the authorization failures or whether my account was subject to any authorization-level restrictions, enhanced monitoring, or internal risk controls. Representatives repeatedly stated the card should work, which proved inaccurate, while failing to disclose material information necessary for me to understand or access my available credit. 

To the extent Avant possesses internal information affecting card usability, including authorization-layer controls, risk flags, or monitoring that restricts transactions despite available credit being displayed, the failure to disclose such information raises potential concerns under the Consumer Financial Protection Act, 12 U.S.C. 5536, which prohibits unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices, including omissions of material information while making representations that an account should function normally. 

Additionally, where internal data or account-level determinations affect a consumers access to credit, the failure to ensure accuracy, transparency, and meaningful disclosure may implicate obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681, including the requirement that information affecting a consumers credit access be handled accurately and disclosed appropriately upon inquiry. 

By repeatedly reciting transaction history without disclosing the true cause of the authorization failures or escalating to a team capable of resolving or explaining the issue, Avant deprived me of meaningful information necessary to understand and use my credit account. This omission materially affected my ability to access credit that was represented as available and in good standing.

Consumer complaint narrative:
TD Bank unfairly processed a check it received for payment from our account before crediting the account with a cash-equivalent deposit made the same day resulting in our account becoming overdrawn and the check return for what it deemed to be insufficient funds in the account. Both the check which caused the overdraft and the deposit that more than sufficiently covered the amount of the check posted to our account the same day. In essence, TD Bank processed the check before crediting the account with the deposit that covered the amount of the check. 
Further Details Explained : We gave our contractor a TD Bank check in the amount of {$14000.00} in the afternoon on XX/XX/year>. The contractor deposited the check into his account that same afternoon. We made a {$20000.00} deposit to our TD Bank account to in the morning that same day to more than cover the amount of the check bringing the account balance to over {$28000.00}. The deposit was a cashiers check for which the funds were drawn from our account at another bank ( we dont have checks to this account ). The funds from the cashiers check should be given the same availability as cash in accordance with applicable Federal regulations. We made every effort to be sure there would be sufficient available funds in the TD Bank account before we gave the contractor a check. In these circumstances, it is reasonable to believe TD Bank would credit our account with the funds from the cashiers check before processing any checks. Indeed, the online account transaction activity showed both the deposit and check posted to the account the same day. To process the deposit and checks in any other order could result in multiple items if presented that day to be returned for insufficient funds and overdraft charges assessed for each item presented for payment. Clearly, such a practice would be not be treating the customer fairly and cause substantial harm. None of the actions taken by TD Bank could be sufficiently explained by a TD Bank customer representative and subsequently a blind transfer to a manager after spending over an hour on the telephone. Neither the customer representative nor the manager could refer me to the appropriate sections of Federal regulations or in the TD Banks Personal Deposit Account Agreement where such a deceptive and abusive practice is permitted.

We have been a customer of TD Bank for well over 20 years and have never overdrawn our account and had checks return for insufficient funds. Clearly, TD Banks practices harmed us and similarly could harm its customers, particularly the elderly and those most vulnerable. We can do something about this unfair practice. We took the time to file this complaint and are closing our accounts at TD Bank.

Evidence of the transaction and are included in the documentation section of this complaint.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing a complaint regarding Citibanks handling of my credit card account, specifically the way my autopay settings were established and maintained in a manner that resulted in repeated interest charges without clear, affirmative consent. 

My account was set to automatically pay a fixed minimum payment of approximately {$35.00} rather than the full statement balance. I did not intentionally choose this setting, and at no point was it clearly disclosed that this autopay configuration would result in ongoing interest charges on a card with a high APR and an annual fee. This setup effectively guaranteed that a balance would be carried and that interest would accrue each billing cycle. 

As a customer who generally pays balances in full and uses autopay specifically to avoid interest, this configuration was materially misleading. Citibank did not provide clear warnings, proactive notifications, or meaningful alerts indicating that I was revolving a balance and incurring interest. The design of this autopay default appears intended to maximize interest revenue rather than protect consumers from unintended debt. 

This issue is particularly problematic given that this is a branded airline credit card marketed on the basis of travel benefits. Once interest charges are incurred, the cards value proposition collapses, yet Citibank continued to allow interest to accrue silently while collecting both interest and an annual fee. 

I believe this constitutes an unfair and deceptive practice, as the autopay system is structured in a way that reasonably leads consumers to believe they are protected from interest when they are not. The lack of clear disclosure and absence of proactive warnings is predatory in effect, even if technically permitted. 

I am requesting : 1. A review of the interest charges applied to my account resulting from this autopay configuration 2. A refund or credit of interest charges assessed during the period in which my account was unknowingly set to minimum-payment autopay 3. Confirmation that my account is now set to pay the full statement balance going forward 4. An explanation of why Citibank allows minimum-payment autopay to be set or maintained without explicit, repeated consumer acknowledgment of the interest consequences I am also requesting that Citibank review its autopay design and disclosure practices to prevent other consumers from being placed into unintended revolving debt.

b'[CFPB Complaint Draft: Defective AdverseAction Notice and Failure to Provide Required ECOA/FCRA Disclosures]

[Reference / FNBO Notice Date: Reference No. XXXX  dated XXXX XXXX XXXXDate mailed to FNBO / Proof of receipt: Mailed via Certified Mail; XXXX  delivery confirmation dated XXXX XXXX XXXX (tracking XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX).
Relief requested: See Requested Relief section below.]
1.) [Summary of complaint]
On XXXX XXXX XXXX FNBO mailed me an adverseaction notice regarding my credit card application (Ref. XXXX). The notice is partially illegible and internally inconsistent, and therefore fails to state the specific principal reasons for the adverse action in a clear, readable manner as required by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B (12 C.F.R. 1002.9). The notice also fails to provide clear, nonmisleading creditscore disclosures and related documentation required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act and Regulation V (15 U.S.C. 1681m; 12 C.F.R. 1022.72). I mailed FNBO a written demand for corrected notices and supporting records; FNBO received that demand on XXXX XXXX XXXX. I ask the CFPB to investigate and require FNBO to provide the relief listed below.

2.)  [Chronology (key dates)]
XXXX FNBO obtained credit score (per FNBO notice).XXXX FNBO mailed adverseaction notice (Ref. XXXX).XXXX I mailed a written demand to FNBO identifying illegibility and requesting corrected notice and records.XXXX XXXX certifiedmail delivery confirmation shows FNBO received my demand.
3. Specific legal deficiencies alleged
A. ECOA / Regulation B (12 C.F.R. 1002.9)

The adverseaction notice must contain a statement of the action taken and either (a) the specific principal reasons for the adverse action or (b) a clear statement of the applicants right to request those reasons. The FNBO notice contains garbled and corrupted text (headings and portions of the reasons section are illegible), preventing a reasonable consumer from identifying the principal reasons for denial. This renders the notice substantively defective and noncompliant with Reg B.

B. FCRA / Regulation V (15 U.S.C. 1681m; 12 C.F.R. 1022.72)

When an adverse action is based in whole or in part on a consumer report or credit score, the user must disclose the credit score, score range, date, provider, and key factors that adversely affected the score. FNBOs notice presents overlapping and ambiguous lists (reasons you did not score well vs. key factors) and fails to clearly tie the score factors to the adverse decision. The presentation is confusing and does not meaningfully explain how the score affected the decision.

C. Consumer Credit Protection Act (FCRA subchapter)

Because FCRA disclosure obligations are part of the Consumer Credit Protection Act framework, FNBOs defective implementation of FCRA disclosures also violates the CCPAs consumerprotection objectives.

D. Record retention and automated decision records

Regulation B and supervisory guidance require creditors to retain application and decision records sufficient to demonstrate compliance. FNBO must preserve and produce automated decision logs, scoring outputs, and model inputs used in my application decision.

4. Harm and why relief is needed
The defective notice deprived me of the ability to understand the principal reasons for denial and to meaningfully exercise my right to obtain a statement of specific reasons or to correct inaccurate information.

The ambiguous score disclosures prevent me from assessing whether the credit decision relied on inaccurate or incomplete information and from disputing errors with the consumer reporting agency or FNBO.

Without the requested records (consumer report copies, scoring output, model name/version, automated decision logs), I cannot verify the accuracy or fairness of FNBOs decision or determine whether systemic problems exist that could harm other consumers.'

Consumer complaint narrative:
THIS IS NOT A DUPLICATE Formal Notice of Continued Procedural Mishandling, Failure to Review Submissions, Improper Duplicate Classification, and Demand for Reopening and Production of Records To Whom It May Concern, I submit this letter to formally document and object to the continued procedural mishandling of my consumer complaints, including indicators that my submissions were not fully reviewed, followed by the improper classification of complaints as duplicates despite the introduction of new material facts and legal issues. 

This correspondence is submitted to preserve the accuracy of the administrative record and to request corrective action consistent with federal law, constitutional due process principles, and CFPB complaint-handling standards. 

1. Indicators of Failure to Review Complaint Submissions During the handling of my complaints, a PNC XXXX XXXX agent instructed me to expect contact from, or remain in communication with, an individual and/or entity : Against whom I had already filed a prior CFPB complaint, and To whom I had already issued a written cease-and-desist directive, both of which were expressly stated in my complaint submissions. 

Had my submissions and complaint history been reviewed in full, such guidance would have conflicted with information already contained in the record. This creates a reasonable inference that my complaints were not substantively reviewed prior to instruction being issued. 

This observation is not presented as an allegation of intent, but as evidence of a procedural failure, not isolated error, inconsistent with CFPB intake and review obligations. 

2. Improper Classification of Complaints as Duplicates Multiple subsequent complaints were later labeled as duplicate despite containing new and material information, including but not limited to : Newly discovered facts concerning defective joint account formation Evidence indicating I was allegedly added as a joint owner while a minor Statements by bank personnel indicating no executed signature or consent exists Branch-level discrepancies and employee-specific conduct Requests for preservation of records ( litigation hold ) Legal reframing from identity theft alone to records accuracy and unlawful account designation Under CFPB standards, complaints that introduce new facts, evidence, or legal theories do not qualify as duplicates. Retroactive consolidation without documented evidentiary review undermines the purpose of the complaint process and deprives the consumer of meaningful consideration. 

This is not a duplicate. Improper misclassification is a continuation of procedural failure and unlawful handling. 

3. Continued Denial of Records to Which I Am Entitled by Law Despite being designated as a joint account holder, I have repeatedly been denied access to records, including : In-person denial of access even when presenting valid government identification Denial of access via telephone Refusal to provide account formation documents, ownership records, or transaction histories As a joint account holderwhether lawfully or defectively designatedI am entitled under federal law to access records reflecting account ownership, formation, and maintenance. 

The continued refusal to provide these records raises concerns under, including but not limited to : The Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments to the U.S. Constitution ( due process ) The Consumer Financial Protection Act ( 12 U.S.C. 5531, 5536 ) The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ), where inaccurate ownership information is maintained or furnished The Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1691 et seq. ), as it relates to lawful account designation and recordkeeping Federal banking law and common-law recordkeeping duties requiring accurate maintenance and disclosure of consumer account records Administrative complaint closure does not negate or suspend these statutory obligations.

3A. Clarification Regarding Records Access and Improper Reliance on Subpoena Standard I further note, in anticipation of a common response, that my request for records is not a subpoena demand, nor does applicable law require a subpoena for a joint account holder to access their own account records. 

My requests are based on statutory consumer access rights and ordinary banking disclosure obligations, not civil discovery standards. 

A subpoena is a litigation tool used to compel production from third parties. It is not a prerequisite for a financial institution or regulator to provide records to an individual who is : Designated as a joint account holder, and/or Allegedly associated with an account for reporting, ownership, or liability purposes If I am treated as a joint owner for any purposewhether reporting, liability, internal coding, or account historythen I am entitled to inspect records supporting that designation without being forced into litigation. 

Requiring a subpoena to access ones own alleged account records would improperly shift the burden to the consumer, undermine statutory access rights, and raise due-process concerns. Administrative complaint closure does not convert statutory access obligations into discretionary discovery matters. 

This clarification is included to ensure the administrative record accurately reflects that my requests are lawful access requests, not discovery demands. 

4. Formal Requests for Corrective Action Accordingly, I respectfully request : 1. Reopening and substantive review of all complaints improperly closed or labeled as duplicates, with full consideration of all new evidence and legal issues 2. Written confirmation that each complaint has been reviewed in full 3. Immediate production of all records to which I am legally entitled, including account formation documents, ownership records, and transaction histories 4. Correction of the administrative record where complaints were misclassified 5. Cessation of premature closures absent documented evidentiary review These requests are consistent with CFPBs statutory mandate to ensure fair, transparent, and accountable handling of consumer complaints.

5. Preservation of Rights Nothing in this correspondence shall be construed as a waiver of any rights or remedies. I expressly reserve all rights under federal and state law. Administrative consolidation or closure of complaints does not preclude judicial review or civil remedies where unlawful conduct is established.

6. Conclusion This matter reflects a continuing procedural failure, not isolated error. This letter is submitted to ensure the administrative record accurately reflects the issues raised and to request corrective action consistent with law. 

I submit this correspondence for inclusion in the administrative record and await an appropriate response consistent with applicable law.

These changes were not clearly or prominently disclosed to me in advance. I later learned that U.S. Bank considers the disclosure to have been made only by embedding a brief notice within a monthly account statement.

Monthly statements are primarily intended to report balances and transaction activity, not to serve as effective notice of material adverse changes to account terms. Embedding such changes within a statement does not provide clear and conspicuous notice and does not give consumers a meaningful opportunity to adjust account behavior to avoid new fees.

I am concerned that this disclosure method represents a broader practice rather than an isolated incident. Implementing material fee and waiver changes while relying on passive disclosure within account statements may prevent consumers from being adequately informed and may raise concerns under consumer protection standards, including unfair or deceptive practices.

I am submitting this complaint to request regulatory review of U.S. Banks disclosure practices related to checking account fee changes.

Immediately after this denial ( within XXXX minutes ), I returned to the pre-approval offer for the same QuickSilver card ( without the bonus ) and accepted it. Capital One approved this application instantly.

Deceptive Advertising ( Bait & Switch ) : It appears the denial was not based on creditworthiness or the stated reason, but solely to avoid paying the advertised acquisition bonus. Using a pretextual credit denial reason to steer a qualified applicant toward a less valuable product is a deceptive practice under the XXXX XXXX.

After waiting 24 hours, I contacted American Express again and was then informed that I needed to wait until an initial delivery attempt was made before a replacement card could be issued. 

As a result, the first card was delivered without my apartment number and was delivered to my building management, where it was placed in a miscellaneous/common package room, making it difficult to retrieve. 

When I retrieved and opened this package, I discovered that the card inside was not the correct or updated card I had requested. I contacted American Express to report this and requested that the correct updated card be sent. During this call, I again clearly and explicitly confirmed my full address, including apartment number XXXX, and was assured the address had been updated. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, following these discussions, a replacement card was issued. During this call, I was again explicitly told on a recorded call that my address had been corrected and that the new card would be sent correctly. 

Despite these repeated confirmations, I later received an email stating that delivery of the replacement card failed due to a missing apartment number, confirming that the address had not been updated as promised. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, after continued delivery issues, I contacted American Express via chat. After speaking with a representative and receiving no resolution, I was placed on hold for a supervisor for over 40 minutes, with the estimated wait time repeatedly increasing. I also called American Express by phone that same day and again received no meaningful resolution. 

After multiple complaints, American Express offered only a {$20.00} statement credit, which does not reasonably reflect the repeated delivery failures, incorrect card issuance, misinformation provided on recorded calls, excessive delays, or the several hours I spent attempting to resolve issues that should have been corrected during the first interaction. 

This experience directly contradicts how the Platinum Card is advertised and marketed. American Express promotes the Platinum Card as offering premium service, priority support, and seamless onboarding. Instead, I experienced repeated agent errors after confirmation, issuance of the wrong card, multiple failed deliveries, and prolonged escalation delays. The gap between the advertised Platinum experience and the service actually delivered is misleading for a premium product with a high annual fee. 

Additionally, the repeated failure to update a simple address detail despite multiple confirmations on recorded calls, combined with the issuance of an incorrect card and continued delivery failures, constitutes operational negligence. Requested Resolution : I am requesting that the CFPB : Investigate Wells Fargos compliance with Regulation CC ( 12 CFR Part 229 ) Require Wells Fargo to explain the basis for the hold and its extension Address Wells Fargos failure to provide required notices Ensure corrective action so that consumers receive proper and timely disclosures going forward

Consumer complaint narrative:
Complaint Narrative I am filing a complaint regarding unfair and misleading interest charges caused by Citibanks payment allocation practices on a credit card account with multiple promotional balance transfers, compounded by inconsistent and contradictory customer service communications.

I had two balance transfers on the same Citibank credit card account : - One balance transfer with a 0 % promotional APR, scheduled to expire on XXXX - A second balance transfer with a 0.99 % promotional APR, which remained active after that date When the 0 % promotional APR expired on XXXX, the APR on that balance increased to approximately 24 %. I made an online payment on XXXX with the clear intent to pay off the balance that had just exited the 0 % promotional period in order to avoid ongoing high-interest charges.

Citibanks online payment system did not allow me to choose which balance my payment would be applied to. Instead, Citibank applied my payment to the lower-APR 0.99 % promotional balance, while leaving the higher-APR balance unpaid. As a result, interest continued to accrue at approximately 24 % on the balance I was actively attempting to eliminate.

This payment allocation defeated my clear and reasonable intent and caused avoidable interest. The payment screen did not clearly disclose that payments could be diverted to a lower-APR promotional balance, nor did it explain how a consumer could prevent post-promotional interest when multiple promotional balances exist.

Customer Service Assurances and Contradictory Written Responses After discovering the issue, I contacted Citibank customer service on three separate occasions. During each call, I was told that the issue would be corrected, that the interest would be adjusted, and that these assurances were documented in the account notes so that any representative could review them.

I specifically asked for confirmation in writing and was repeatedly told that written confirmation was unnecessary because the resolution was documented internally in Citibanks system notes.

Despite these assurances, I later received written letters from Citibank stating the opposite, denying that any correction could be made. These letters directly contradicted the verbal assurances I relied upon. Copies of these letters are attached to this complaint. I am also attaching call log screenshots showing the dates and frequency of my calls to Citibank customer service.

Due to Citibanks failure to resolve this issue and the continued accrual of interest, I ultimately closed the account. After closure, I no longer have online access to view the detailed interest calculations or statements. I have requested copies of my statements from Citibank for the relevant billing periods and will be provided upon receipt.

Contradictory and Misleading Payment Allocation Explanation Please note that even Citibanks written responses contains internally contradictory language regarding how payments are applied.

The letter states that : Each month 's minimum payment due is applied to principal balances in APR order from lowest to highest.

The letter then states : Payment amounts greater than the minimum due are applied to balances with higher APRs before balances with lower rates.

My payment exceeded the minimum due. At the time of payment, one balance carried an APR of approximately 24 %, while the other carried a 0.99 % promotional APR. Under Citibanks own written explanation, my payment should have been applied to the higher-APR balance first.

Instead, Citibank applied my payment to the lower-APR balance and continued charging high interest, then relied on this same explanation to state it was unable to apply [ my ] payment as requested. This contradiction made it impossible for me to reasonably understand how to avoid post-promotional interest.

Why This Is Unfair and Deceptive - Citibanks payment allocation practices were not clearly disclosed, particularly in a multi-promotion scenario.

- The online payment system did not allow consumers to direct payments to the highest-interest balance - I relied on repeated verbal assurances that the issue would be corrected - Citibanks written responses directly contradicted those assurances- Citibanks own written explanation of payment allocation is internally inconsistent - I incurred avoidable interest despite acting promptly and in good faith Taken together, this constitutes an unfair and deceptive practice, especially when combined with inconsistent customer service representations and a lack of transparent disclosure.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am submitting this complaint regarding Synchrony Banks reduction of my credit limit immediately after I utilized my credit line following direct marketing and solicitation from Synchrony. 

Synchrony actively marketed and encouraged me to use my available credit. In reliance on this solicitation, I used the credit line as promoted. Shortly thereafter, Synchrony reduced my credit limit to reflect approximately 90 % utilization, which materially increased my utilization ratio and caused a steep decline in my credit score. 

Synchrony advised that this adverse action was based on an automated algorithm citing the following factors : Bank card balance-to-income ratio Allegedly insufficient payment amounts Loan balances This constitutes an adverse action under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681a ( k ), and triggers specific notice, accuracy, and disclosure obligations.

The stated reasons for the adverse action are inconsistent with my documented credit profile and raise concerns regarding compliance with FCRA 1681e ( b ) and 1681m ( a ) : My credit report reflects 100 % on-time payments across all credit accounts All payments on the Synchrony account were made on time and in amounts exceeding the contractual minimum Over the past XXXX years, I have had no delinquencies, late payments, or defaults My loan balances are either paid as agreed or deferred until XXXX, with no current payment obligation Additionally, Synchrony has issued new lines of credit and approved new credit accounts during this same period, which directly contradicts the assertion that my credit profile presents elevated risk. This inconsistency raises concerns regarding the accuracy, integrity, and reasonable procedures used to evaluate consumer creditworthiness, as required under FCRA 1681e ( b ).

Synchrony stated that a notice letter was sent to inform me of the credit line reduction ; however, the letter arrived several days after the adverse action had already occurred. This delayed notification raises concerns regarding compliance with FCRA 1681m ( a ), which requires timely notice of adverse actions, including the specific reasons for the action and the consumers rights regarding the use of consumer report information. 

The timing and nature of the decision indicate that the action was implemented through automated decision-making without meaningful human review, individualized assessment, or verification of accurate and current data. Such practices undermine the consumer protections embedded in the FCRA and increase the risk of inaccurate or unfair outcomes. 

I am a XXXX  mother supporting XXXX children through college. At times, this requires responsible use of available credit. My long-standing payment history demonstrates disciplined financial management and a low-risk profile. Penalizing a consumer for utilizing credit immediately after being encouraged to do sodespite perfect payment historyraises serious concerns regarding fairness, transparency, and compliance. 

As a result of Synchronys actions, I experienced : Artificially inflated utilization A significant and avoidable decline in my credit score Reduced access to credit despite responsible account management I respectfully request that the CFPB review Synchronys practices for compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act and UDAAP standards, and require appropriate corrective action, including : Reconsideration and restoration of my prior credit limit based on accurate payment performance Clear disclosure of the consumer report data and criteria used in the adverse decision Confirmation that deferred loan obligations are accurately reflected in underwriting Assurance that adverse actions are supported by reasonable procedures, meaningful human review, and timely notice as required by the FCRA Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX, Michigan XXXX XXXX XXXX

Under XXXX card network rules for disputes of this amount, merchants must provide proof that goods were delivered to and received by the cardholder or an authorized recipient. Unattended delivery to an unsecured common area does not satisfy this requirement. No signature was obtained. I never received the merchandise. 
I confirmed with neighbors and building management that no one received this package. The package was either stolen from the unsecured lobby or was never actually left there. 

Evidence I Have : Email from Merchant dated XX/XX/year>, confirming unattended lobby delivery Confirmation that my building lobby is publicly accessible Confirmation from neighbors and building management that package was not received Wells Fargo 's Error : Wells Fargo failed to apply the correct card network standards for delivery verification. They accepted insufficient evidence from the merchant and incorrectly closed my dispute. For a {$380.00} purchase, card network rules require actual proof of receipt by the cardholder or authorized person, not merely tracking showing delivery to a building address. 
This is a clear violation of the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 USC 1666, Regulation Z ) which requires creditors to properly investigate billing errors including charges for merchandise not received. 

What I Want : Wells Fargo to re-open my dispute investigation Wells Fargo to apply correct card network delivery verification standards Permanent reversal of the {$380.00} charge Confirmation that this dispute will not negatively impact my credit or account standing I sent a formal rebuttal letter to Wells Fargo on XX/XX/year>, but am filing this CFPB complaint simultaneously because Wells Fargo 's incorrect application of card network rules has caused me financial harm.

Overview The furnishers response dated XX/XX/XXXX ( transmitted weeks later ) asserts that the accounts reporting was confirmed as accurate. That assertion is demonstrably false.

That overpayment necessarily carried forward to satisfy the XX/XX/XXXX payment obligation. XXXX therefore can not be treated as an unpaid or newly delinquent month under the payment plan. 

Ignoring the carry-forward effect of this overpayment while selectively reassigning payments backward is improper and inflates delinquency. 



XXXX. False Claim of Underpayment in XX/XX/XXXX The furnisher asserts that payments from XXXX forward were short, beginning with XXXX. This is false. 

XX/XX/XXXX payments : {$120.00} {$34.00} Total XXXX payments : {$150.00} This amount exceeded the reduced payment obligation. XXXX was not underpaid and can not be treated as delinquent. 



XXXX. XXXX Overpayment and XX/XX/XXXX Payment The XXXX overpayment necessarily carried forward to offset the XXXX obligation. 

Additionally : XX/XX/XXXX payment : {$75.00} ( made and accepted ) When XXXX overpayment and XXXX accepted payment are properly applied, XXXX can not be treated as a qualifying delinquency month. 



XXXX. Improper Reliance on PostCharge-Off Activity The furnisher relies on XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX payments to characterize delinquency and justify charge-off.

Per credit bureau reporting, the account was charged off on XX/XX/XXXX. Once an account is charged off : It can no longer accrue delinquency months Postcharge-off payments are not plan payments Postcharge-off months can not be used to justify the charge-off Using XXXX activity to rationalize a XXXX charge-off is invalid.

Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am submitting this complaint regarding Bank of Americas improper denial of a dispute involving an {$8000.00} unauthorized transaction on my credit card account. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, when I first became aware of the transaction, it was still pending. I immediately contacted Bank of America and informed the representative that the charge was not authorized and was not made by me. During this call, I was explicitly told that the transaction had been canceled and I was reassured that it would not go through, as it was reported as unauthorized while still pending. 

Despite these clear assurances, Bank of America allowed the transaction to post to my account. 

I subsequently reopened the claim multiple times. Bank of America ultimately denied the dispute, stating that the transaction was made using one of my verified devices and relying on merchant documentation that allegedly includes a signature. That signature is not mine, and I dispute its authenticity. 

The transaction was initiated by my former partner, who had access to my device and financial information through deception and coercive circumstances. Bank of America is improperly equating device access with authorization, which does not meet the legal standard for an authorized transaction.

Bank of Americas handling of this matter appears inconsistent with the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) and Regulation E, including but not limited to the following : Under Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005.2 ( m ) ), an electronic fund transfer is unauthorized when initiated by a person without actual authority, even if access to a device or account was obtained.

I provided timely notice of the unauthorized transaction while it was still pending, triggering the banks duty to investigate and take appropriate action.

I relied on Bank of Americas explicit representation that the transaction was canceled and would not post. Allowing the charge to proceed after such representation constitutes bank error and misrepresentation. 

The denial relies on device association rather than evidence of actual consumer authorization. 

Bank of America failed to reasonably address the forged signature contained in the merchant documentation.

By denying this claim under these circumstances, Bank of America failed to conduct a Regulation Ecompliant investigation and failed to account for bank error arising from its initial assurances.

I am requesting that Bank of America : 1. Conduct a proper supervisory review compliant with Regulation E 2. Acknowledge the bank error and misrepresentation related to the assurance that the transaction was canceled 3. Reverse the {$8000.00} unauthorized transaction and make my account whole 4. Ensure that no negative credit reporting results from this disputed charge while it is under review I am attaching Bank of Americas denial letter dated XX/XX/year>, and I am prepared to provide a sworn affidavit confirming that the signature is not mine and that I did not authorize this transaction.

2. Why Bank of Americas Conduct Is Improper and Potentially Unlawful A. Unlawful Retention of Cleared Check Deposit Funds ( UCC Article 4 ) Under Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) Article 4, once a deposited check has cleared, a bank has a duty to either : Make the funds available, or Return the funds to the customer upon account closure A bank does not have authority to hold cleared check funds for months without a court order, legal seizure, or statutory requirement. 
Bank of America has provided no legal order or documentation authorizing the retention of my {$47000.00} check deposit. 

B. Improper Use of Risk or Merchant Review to Justify Holding Non-Merchant Funds Even if a bank is reviewing merchant activity, it can not lawfully withhold unrelated customer funds. Holding non-merchant funds under the justification of a merchant review constitutes an unfair and abusive practice under : 12 U.S.C. 5531 ( Consumer Financial Protection Act UDAAP ) C. Violation of FDIC Account Closure and Funds Disbursement Standards FDIC supervisory guidance requires that when an account is closed : Remaining funds must be returned promptly Funds may not be held indefinitely without lawful authority A blanket statement that funds will be held for at least six months without providing a legal basis violates these standards.

D. Failure to Provide Written Legal Justification or Adverse Action Notice Bank of America has failed to provide : A written explanation citing the specific law allowing a six-month hold Any adverse action notice Any documentation of a lawful investigation requiring retention of funds This lack of disclosure violates federal consumer protection expectations and constitutes a deceptive and abusive practice.

Harm Caused As a result of Bank of Americas actions : My business is deprived of {$87000.00} in operating funds {$47000.00} of my own deposited money is being held without legal justification The account is closed, yet funds are withheld I am unable to operate my business or meet obligations 4. On XX/XX/year>, I paid {$21000.00} via Discover to XXXX XXXX for a 14-day luxury, fully guided tour of XXXX for myself, my wife, and my daughter. The total cost of the tour was approximately {$22000.00}, with the remaining balance paid using other credit cards. The tour began on XX/XX/year>.

In addition, multiple excursions and activities listed in the itinerary as included were not booked or paid for by XXXX XXXX, and we were required to self-pay for some activities and meals that were explicitly listed as included and to be covered by the guide.

These failures represent substantial non-performance of the contracted services. I have provided an itemized, day-by-day list detailing the missing guides, excursions, activities, and services.

Throughout the trip, we were in direct contact with the owner of XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and repeatedly notified her of the missing services. On XX/XX/year>, she explicitly acknowledged these failures and agreed in writing to refund us for both the missing guide services and the unprovided excursions, activities, and meals. Most of our correspondence with the owner occurred via XXXX. Because these messages can not be forwarded, screenshots were provided as documentation. I can not provide them here since they are larger than XXXX XXXX.

Consumer complaint narrative:
A Wells Fargo credit card with a credit limit of approximately {$3000.00} was opened in my name without my knowledge, consent, or authorization. I did not apply for this account, did not use the card, and did not knowingly authorize any charges or payments associated with it. I did not receive account disclosures or billing statements and was unaware the account existed. 

I first became aware of this fraudulent account on XX/XX/year>, when a Wells Fargo banker informed me that the credit card was open. I disputed the account immediately upon discovery. Until that date, I had no knowledge that such an account existed. 

Wells Fargo denied my fraud claim on the grounds that monthly payments of approximately {$36.00} were being made. This conclusion is incorrect. These payments were automatic withdrawals from my bank account and were not knowingly made or affirmatively authorized by me with awareness of the account. Automatic debits do not constitute authorization, consent, or ownership of a credit card account. 

This matter is account-opening identity theft, not a billing dispute. Mail related to this account was sent to an address not under my control, and after my accounts were previously compromised, I restricted online banking access. These factors explain why the fraudulent account remained undiscovered until XX/XX/year>. 

I have filed an official Identity Theft Report with the Federal Trade Commission. Despite this, Wells Fargo has failed to properly investigate the identity theft and has improperly relied on automatic payments as evidence that no fraud occurred. 

I am requesting CFPB assistance to require Wells Fargo to recognize this account as fraudulent identity theft, refund all funds withdrawn from my bank account in connection with this account ( including all automatic payments, interest, and fees ), permanently close the account as fraudulent, correct any related credit reporting, and provide written confirmation of full resolution.

Consumer complaint narrative:
My Capital One credit card account was closed without prior written notice and subsequently placed into internal collections, leaving me without any reasonable repayment options despite my willingness to pay. 

I did not receive any notices of returned payments, delinquency, account closure, adverse action, or placement into collections. To date, the only correspondence I have received has been routine billing statements reflecting the balance due. I did not receive emails, text messages, phone calls, or mailed correspondence notifying me of any serious issues with the account, the closure itself, or the change to collections status. 

During an extended period of medical hardship that prevented me from working for over a year. Despite financial strain, payments were made consistently. On some occasions, payments were returned due to timing and cash flow constraints, not refusal to pay, and those payments were later made manually as funds became available. At no point did I intentionally stop paying or abandon the obligation. 

After learning that the account had been closed and was in collections, I paused payments briefly in order to obtain clarification, as I was unable to get clear information from Capital One regarding what had occurred or what options were available. This pause was done in good faith and with the intention of resuming payments once accurate information could be obtained. 

I contacted Capital One multiple times seeking assistance and requesting a structured repayment plan or hardship option. I was told by multiple representatives and a supervisor that because the account was closed, no hardship or forbearance options were available, no escalation was possible, and my only options were to continue making payments while interest accrues indefinitely or wait for the account to be transferred to third-party collections. 

I am willing and able to repay this debt under reasonable terms. However, continued interest accrual and high required payment amounts make repayment under the current structure financially unsustainable. I have sufficient funds to make consistent monthly payments if interest is temporarily reduced or suspended so that payments reduce the principal balance. 

Additionally, upon closure of the account, all accumulated rewards points were forfeited without prior notice. This card was obtained and used in large part for its rewards program, and the loss of those points further compounded the impact of the sudden closure. 

I am requesting that Capital One review this account for a reasonable repayment plan with temporary interest relief, or provide a written explanation as to why no such option exists, given my willingness to repay and the lack of notice provided.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Regulation E Violations Bank Failed to Provide Required Documentation and Failed to Issue Provisional Credit. 

This complaint is not about the original dispute, but about SoFi Banks repeated violations of Regulation E during the dispute process. The bank did not follow the requirements of 12 CFR 1005.11 and denied my rights under EFTA.

1. SoFi did not provide the documents they used in their investigation.

Violation : 12 CFR 1005.11 ( d ) I asked twice for the documents they relied on to deny my dispute, and they still have not provided anything. Regulation E requires the bank to give the consumer copies of the documents they used. Without this, I can not verify whether their investigation was valid.

2. SoFi failed to issue provisional credit for one of the transactions.

Violation : 12 CFR 1005.11 ( c ) ( 2 ) ( i ) The {$800.00} dispute was not resolved within 10 business days, and they never issued provisional credit. Regulation E requires provisional credit when the investigation is not completed in time. This requirement is not optional.

3. SoFi used the fact that my card was in my possession to deny the claim, which is not allowed.

Violation : 12 CFR 1005.2 ( m ) Regulation E makes it clear that a transaction can be unauthorized even if the card is in the consumers possession. SoFi treated card-present as proof of authorization, which is not legally correct.

4. The bank tried to restart the Regulation E timeline by asking for additional information after they had already made a decision. 
Violation : 12 CFR 1005.11 ( c ) ( 1 ) The clock for the investigation starts when the consumer reports the error. The bank can not extend or reset the timeline by requesting unnecessary information after an initial decision. This delayed the investigation and delayed provisional credit.

5. They changed the dispute type without my consent.

Violation : 12 CFR 1005.11 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( ii ) Expecting to be charged {$100.00} does not authorize {$150.00}. SoFi reclassified my dispute based on my explanation, but that does not change the fact that the higher amount was not authorized.

6. SoFis investigation was not reasonable.

Violation : 12 CFR 1005.11 ( c ) ( 1 ) Rather than provide actual evidence, they referenced irrelevant facts like me logging into my account days before the transaction. That does not prove authorization or resolve whether an error occurred. A reasonable investigation requires reviewing merchant data and transaction evidence, which they did not provide. 

I raised these issues in a prior complaint, but the bank still refuses to provide documentation or issue provisional credit. I am filing this new complaint specifically for the Regulation E violations listed above. 

I am requesting that the CFPB require SoFi Bank to : Provide all documentation relied upon in their investigation Issue full provisional credit for both disputed transactions as required Reinvestigate the matter in compliance with Regulation E Because these issues involve repeated violations of Regulation E, the failure to provide required documentation, and the failure to issue mandatory provisional credit under 1005.11 ( c ) ( 2 ) ( i ), I am asking for supervisory escalation of this complaint. I have attempted to resolve this matter directly with the bank, and the previous CFPB complaint did not result in compliance. These violations continue to cause financial harm, and the bank has not followed federal requirements. I am requesting that this complaint be reviewed at the supervisory level for enforcement of Regulation E. 

Thank you.

Issue: Problem with a lender or other company charging your account
Consumer complaint narrative:
I am disputing XXXX ACH debits from my SoFi account in the amounts of {$1000.00} and {$8700.00} related to a solar installation contract. 
I have a written contract with the merchant that explicitly states payment is authorized only after permitting is obtained. Permitting was never obtained. No services were rendered, no equipment was delivered, and no work was initiated. 

Despite this, the merchant initiated ACH debits against my account.

I timely disputed the transactions with SoFi and provided the written contract showing the conditional authorization and the merchants complete failure to perform.

Banks response : SoFi denied my claim and stated that this is a civil dispute involving service quality or non-receipt and therefore outside the scope of the ACH networks rules. SoFi refused to credit my account and closed the matter.

I submitted multiple written rebuttals clarifying that this is not a service quality or non-receipt dispute. No services were provided at all, and the contractual condition authorizing payment was never satisfied. I also requested escalation to SoFis ACH/back-office compliance team. SoFi maintained its denial. 

Why this is a regulatory issue : This dispute is not about dissatisfaction with services. It is an authorization failure. 
Under XXXX Rule XXXX, an ACH debit must be authorized and must conform to the terms of the authorization. In this case, authorization was expressly conditioned on permitting, which never occurred. As a result, the merchant did not have authority to initiate the debits. 

This places the transactions within XXXX return eligibility, including XXXX ( Entry Not in Accordance With Terms of Authorization ) and potentially XXXX ( Unauthorized Debit ). 

SoFis denial appears to rely on a categorical misclassification of the dispute as a civil matter, without addressing whether the ACH debits complied with the authorization terms. Treating an authorization violation as a service quality dispute improperly narrows the scope of the banks investigation. 

Supporting documentation available : Written solar contract showing payment conditional on permitting Proof that no permitting was obtained Proof that no services were rendered SoFi denial correspondence Written rebuttals requesting escalation

WFBNA CARD Address XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, IA XXXX Phone number ( XXXX ) XXXX Record details On record until XX/XX/XXXX Inquired on XX/XX/XXXX Comment Unspecified. This inquiry is scheduled to continue on record until XX/XX/XXXX. 

This is a clear and flagrant violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.

A company can only pull ( procure or obtain ) your consumer report if it has a permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. 1681b. Common permissible purposes include : a credit transaction you initiated ( application for credit/loan ), account review of an existing account, insurance underwriting, certain employment purposes ( with specific disclosures/authorization requirements ), and some legitimate business needs tied to a transaction you initiated.

If there was no permissible purpose, it can be an FCRA violation. The company can face civil liability for negligent noncompliance ( 15 U.S.C. 1681o ) or willful noncompliance ( 15 U.S.C. 1681n ), which can include actual damages, statutory damages ( for willful violations ), punitive damages ( for willful violations ), and attorneys fees.
